Russia Says Investors Will Bear Losses From Foreign Stablecoin Freezes; Crypto Holdings Reach $44B According to TASS, Russia has around 20 million crypto users with total holdings estimated at RUB 3.7 trillion ($44 billion), while daily crypto transaction volume stands at roughly RUB 50 billion ($595 million), Deputy Finance Minister Ivan Chebeskov said. Chebeskov said Russian tax residents will be required to report crypto transactions conducted outside the country’s regulated framework to the Federal Tax Service. If foreign issuers freeze assets such as USDT or USDC for reasons beyond the control of Russian depositories, investors will bear the resulting losses. — link

Binance to Rebrand Funding Account to 'Stocks Account' Binance will begin a phased migration of cryptocurrency assets from user Funding Accounts to Spot Accounts starting September 29, 2026, a process expected to run through January 2027, after which the Funding Account will be officially rebranded as the "Stocks Account" dedicated exclusively to the clearing and settlement of equities and stock options. Under this arrangement, on-chain deposits into Funding Accounts will be disabled effective September 29, and the renamed Stocks Account will support six settlement assets (USD, USDC, USDT, USD1, U, and BNB) for stock trading, while deposits and withdrawals for all other crypto assets will route exclusively through Spot Accounts; users can proactively transfer their holdings beforehand via a new "One-Click Migration" feature, with any remaining balances automatically migrated in batches by the system starting in January 2027 without affecting total asset values or security. — link

Bitcoin Spot ETFs Recorded a Total Net Inflow of $715 Million on September 22 According to SoSoValue data, U.S. Bitcoin spot ETFs recorded a total net inflow of $715 million on September 22 (Eastern Time), marking four consecutive days of net inflows. Meanwhile, Ethereum spot ETFs saw a total net inflow of $162 million yesterday, extending their net inflow streak to three consecutive days. — link

Highlight Clip: Tether Co-Founder: What Is the Most Important Feature of Next-Generation Stablecoins? Tether Co-Founder: What Is the Most Important Feature of Next-Generation Stablecoins? Tether co-founder Reeve Collins said in an interview with Wu Blockchain that next-generation stablecoins will move toward “Stablecoin 2.0,” with reserve assets becoming fully transparent on-chain, yield separated from the stablecoin itself, and programmable mechanisms enabling precise distribution to liquidity providers and participants in distribution channels. He believes artificial intelligence will reshape the financial industry, while blockchain, stablecoins, and underlying protocols will increasingly operate in the background, enabling real-time settlement of global value and funds. — link
